correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact hitting transform r(z)^a and walk Green function u(z)r(z)^|k|, reflection at first hit of a gives P(S_j=0,M_j≥a)=P(S_j=2a). Splitting at every j≥1 return and future hitting event gives the stated three geometric sums for E[M_n L_n], with the exclusion of S0. As z→1, u~(2(1−z))^−1/2, 1−r~sqrt(2(1−z)), and weights (1+1/2−1/3)=7/6 yield leading 7/12·(1−z)^−2; nonnegative monotone moments justify monotone Tauberian E[M_nL_n]/n→7/12. Return-count second-moment transform ((u−1)(2u−1))/(1−z) and Donsker/Doob uniform integrability give each normalized variance 1−2/π. Thus Cov/n=7/12−2/π<0 and Corr ratio as claimed. Independent exact-fraction dynamic programming of all (position,maximum,return-count) states and separate binomial/Catalan coefficient expansion agree for every n≤16 on three moments, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge statement-level comparison of the precise functor, object and parameter with relevant full-text primary sources and published mathematical results. A bivariate generating-function derivative of the joint distribution of maximum and zero-local-time, an excursion decomposition and Brownian maximum–local-time scaling may be alternative formulations. The specific time-discrete mixed Green/first-hitting transform is tested directly, not inferred from a title match. Spitzer-type maximum/endpoint transforms, classical Lévy identities and joint Brownian local-time laws are stronger frameworks in neighboring variables, but the accessible papers inspected do not explicitly establish this discrete same-path M_n L_n GF with origin-return normalization. Kirschenhofer–Prodinger 1996 gives return counts and number of visits to the running maximum (not height×zero returns). Resultary published symmetry identity concerns maximum×odd terminal-point functions, not the pathwise accumulated L_n. No exact precomputed M_nL_n coefficient table in those inspected sources; historical broader bivariate transform remains a real risk. No function g(S_n) equals L_n for a given path: two trajectories can have identical endpoints but different return counts, so the endpoint covariance law does not imply the current covariance. A complete max/local-time joint distribution, if located, would imply the mixed GF and could overturn originality; none verified in inspected sources. Any remaining bibliography uncertainty is retained as residual risk, not presented as novelty proof.
residual_risks: A classical Spitzer–Lévy or excursion-theoretic full joint maximum/local-time transform might imply the mixed coefficient; accessible Kirschenhofer–Prodinger was read, but exhaustive historical exclusion is impossible.
